development_note: declared before any rustc run of these files and before any T code. Before declaring, the T baseline, the comment-fence candidate CLI (SHA-256 3960ec9069c910fbb832b580299b2a7c2ec73b45c7af8f47a00569374504c24c, built from 1aa288ad1) made two kinds of pre-T checks, recorded in obj/parallel/array-types/{twins,client-twins}. (1) It exported the provider and the generated controls, giving the `before` texts below. (2) It compiled each client as a client of the pointer-slices provider packet, with the T provider's authored array section moved into the client crate without `pub` and without its two [T; N] impls (they would be orphans there) and without `copied`, which needs them: values, generic, fields and wide ran natively to 42, and wrong-length, wrong-element, moved and wide-length gave the client_shape_twin texts below. No twin of the full provider is possible before T, because the baseline cannot export any array row and a source-core library is checked only through its export
rule: integrator-approved B2 slice T under Lane C's T1-T6: version thirteen's type recipe tag 14, `14 | element | term`, with K's const term `0 | ty | bits(16 B LE)` or `1 | slot`, admitted only under body_nodes() and emitted only through recipe_emission::type_row. The term is written in place and read into a dense cold `array_lengths` column in type-row order. A value term's ty is exactly the usize row and its bits are canonical for usize; a slot term names a usize const parameter. A value folds to the consumer's Kind::Array and a slot to Kind::ArrayTerm, so each array type has one wire form. Each consumer proves the element sized from its own facts. T owns whole-value Read, Store and copy of array-typed places; list and repeat rvalues, indexing, element patterns, unsizing, general CoerceUnsized and core's array/mod.rs impls stay with Lane C's arrays item
